name: js-fitz/STR-Monitor
what_it_holds: Multi-file panel for monitoring Boston's 2019 Short-Term Rental Ordinance: airbnb.csv (23 merged Inside Airbnb scrapes, 124,730 rows x 31 cols, Jan 2017-Nov 2019, listing IDs/prices/host info/license status), STRE.csv (city STR public registry keyed by SAM_ID, 396,462 rows x 16 cols, registration status + violation counts, downloaded Feb 2020), STR_apps.csv (2,127 rows x 25 cols, internal STR license-application tracker from Boston's Dept of Innovation & Technology, license numbers/status/issue dates), SAMREF.csv (396,462 rows x 43 cols, address/GPS reference), bari_props_2019.csv (174,074 rows x 94 cols, Boston Area Research Initiative property assessment/land-use/owner-occupancy data), and padmapper.csv (917,948 rows x 6 cols, 87 merged scrapes of long-term rental asking prices, Jan 2016-Mar 2020).
why_useful: Directly fills gap #1 (historical/archived Inside Airbnb dumps pre-2023 — Boston 2015-2019 vintage we do not hold) and gap #12 (city STR registration/ordinance enforcement dataset). Also touches gap #13 (Padmapper long-term-rental listings for STR/LTR host-supply crossover). A real natural experiment (ordinance date, enforcement date, before/after listing counts) that could anchor an elasticity estimate for regulation impact on supply.
size_hint: 124,730 listing rows; 917,948 LTR rows; 174,074 parcels; 396,462 addresses
themes: STR regulation trackers and ordinance datasets: city STR law databases, Legistar/LegiScan clients, EU parliament open data, court records (CourtListener/RECAP) on Airbnb litigation
Housing-policy and STR-ban datasets: HOA/condo STR bans, NYC OSE enforcement data, Barcelona/Amsterdam/Paris enforcement, Spanish 2025 platform registration numbers
why_all: Directly fills gap #1 (historical/archived Inside Airbnb dumps pre-2023 — Boston 2015-2019 vintage we do not hold) and gap #12 (city STR registration/ordinance enforcement dataset). Also touches gap #13 (Padmapper long-term-rental listings for STR/LTR host-supply crossover). A real natural experiment (ordinance date, enforcement date, before/after listing counts) that could anchor an elasticity estimate for regulation impact on supply.

A full worked example of matching a city STR license registry + enforcement/violation counts + application pipeline to Inside Airbnb listings and long-term rental comps around a real STR ordinance (owner-occupancy requirement, per-night fines). Directly analogous to the HOA/condo STR-ban and municipal-registration angle in the theme; the STRE/STR_apps registry design is a template for building a similar panel for other cities (e.g., Barcelona/Amsterdam/Paris licensing) even though the data itself is Boston-only and stops in 2020.

name: datanews/illegal-hotel-inspections
what_it_holds: inspections.csv, one row per inspection, 2,684 inspection records (~2,491 after excluding 193 unrelated reports) from NYC Mayor's Office of Special Enforcement (OSE), obtained via FOIL/FOIA request by WNYC. Fields cover property details, inspection rationale, and identified violations for illegal short-term-rental activity. Date range October 2013 through April 2015. Originated as Word docs, converted to HTML, parsed to CSV.
why_useful: Direct hit on the NYC OSE enforcement keyword hint in the theme brief; a rare committed, structured extract of actual OSE inspection/violation records rather than a news summary. Old vintage (2013-2015, pre-Local Law 18) limits direct use for a 2026 forecast, but it is a template for what an OSE FOIL pull looks like and could be combined with a fresher FOIL request if the team wants a current NYC enforcement proxy for STR supply suppression.
themes: Housing-policy and STR-ban datasets: HOA/condo STR bans, NYC OSE enforcement data, Barcelona/Amsterdam/Paris enforcement, Spanish 2025 platform registration numbers
why_all: Direct hit on the NYC OSE enforcement keyword hint in the theme brief; a rare committed, structured extract of actual OSE inspection/violation records rather than a news summary. Direct historical NYC OSE enforcement microdata (this scout's core target and gap #12 regulatory tracker). Pre-dates our held NYC OSE dataset and could extend the enforcement-intensity time series further back (2013-15), useful as a base-period comparator for post-Local-Law-18 enforcement intensity.

name: str-regulation-housing
what_it_holds: ETH Zurich master's thesis (2024) replication package, 'Regulatory Repercussions: how municipal short-term rental regulation affects US housing costs'. Two committed CSVs: regulatory_data.csv (131 US cities across 44 states, coded municipal STR-ordinance 'prohibitiveness scores' 0.5-5.0 covering hosted vs. unhosted rental rules and enforcement mechanisms) and longitudinal_data.csv (2,431 city-month panel rows, 24 California cities, 2015-2023, combining prohibitiveness scores with rental costs, property values, and demographic/economic covariates). Codebooks included; raw ordinance PDFs and MAXQDA project not included but coded results are. MIT licensed.
why_useful: Strong direct hit on gap #12 (STR ordinance tracker / city registration datasets, US-wide with a quantified prohibitiveness score across 131 cities/44 states) and gap #13 (STR-housing-cost crossover panel, CA cities 2015-2023) -- a genuinely new, committed, structured dataset outside anything we currently hold.
geography: United States (131 cities/44 states regulatory panel; 24 California cities longitudinal panel)
time_coverage: 2015-2023 (longitudinal panel); regulatory panel is current as coded (2024 thesis)
duplicate_of_holding: not a duplicate; new to our regulatory event database (32 factors) -- longer time span and quantified score, worth cross-checking against our existing 32-factor database for overlap/extension
themes: UPGo (McGill) and strr R package: STR research tooling and datasets for Canada/US cities
wildcard: an urban economist studying platform housing effects who kno
why_all: Strong direct hit on gap #12 (STR ordinance tracker / city registration datasets, US-wide with a quantified prohibitiveness score across 131 cities/44 states) and gap #13 (STR-housing-cost crossover panel, CA cities 2015-2023) -- a genuinely new, committed, structured dataset outside anything we currently hold.

A directly usable, longer (2015-2023) and methodologically rigorous companion to gap #12/#13 (STR-ordinance-to-housing-cost pass-through); the prohibitiveness score is a continuous alternative to the letter-grade regulatory classifications we currently score as ±0.5 intervals, and the DiD template is reusable for any of our own city-ban events.

name: str-regulation-data (STR Rule Watch)
what_it_holds: Human-verified US short-term-rental regulation dataset, 176 markets (116 cities, 10 counties, all 50 states). CSV one-row-per-market summary plus JSON per-market records with permit requirements/fees, occupancy rules, stay-length limits, lodging taxes, an 8-level regulatory-status categorical (allowed_no_permit -> banned), verbatim source-quote evidence and last-verified dates. CC-BY-4.0, updated 2026-07-30, live counterpart at shortrentalrules.com.
why_useful: Finer-grained and more current than our 32-factor regulatory event database and the ~25-dataset municipal registry panel (gap #12); a clean cross-sectional status variable for the 4Q26 regional-mix and North America nights bridge, and a candidate control set for any city-level STR natural-experiment work.
time_coverage: current snapshot, dated verification fields back several years per market
themes: wildcard: an urban economist studying platform housing effects who kno
why_all: Finer-grained and more current than our 32-factor regulatory event database and the ~25-dataset municipal registry panel (gap #12); a clean cross-sectional status variable for the 4Q26 regional-mix and North America nights bridge, and a candidate control set for any city-level STR natural-experiment work.

name: nycOpenData (rOpenSci)
what_it_holds: R package giving programmatic access to any NYC Open Data Socrata dataset (search/filter/download), including the city's own short-term-rental registration dataset published by the Mayor's Office of Special Enforcement under Local Law 18.
why_useful: Generic but working method to pull NYC's OSE short-term-rental registration counts/records over time (registrations fell from ~38,000 at start of 2023 to ~3,000 by 2026), which is a direct, point-in-time-able proxy for NYC STR supply through the LL18 transition — complements rather than duplicates Inside Airbnb listing snapshots.
geography: New York City (any NYC Open Data dataset)
time_coverage: live pull; historical depth depends on dataset revision history on the portal
duplicate_of_holding: adjacent to, not the same as, the existing '25 municipal STR registries incl. NYC OSE' holding — this is a generic access tool rather than a stored NYC OSE dataset
themes: Inside Airbnb New York City snapshots around Local Law 18 (2023-06 to 2024-03) stored in repos
why_all: Generic but working method to pull NYC's OSE short-term-rental registration counts/records over time (registrations fell from ~38,000 at start of 2023 to ~3,000 by 2026), which is a direct, point-in-time-able proxy for NYC STR supply through the LL18 transition — complements rather than duplicates Inside Airbnb listing snapshots.
